newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa ends lower, switches active.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa ends lower, switches active.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures ended modestly lower on Monday, pressured by an afternoon round of speculative selling, floor sources said.

Closing volume was extremely heavy, at an estimated 27,025 lots, just shy of the CSCE record of 27,681 lots. Traders attributed the bulk of the turnover to brisk switch trading, with one trade house crossing 7,000 lots of March/March 1997.

"The interesting point is that the volume did not translate into a larger price move. People are reluctant to be aggressive on the short or long side," said Prudential Securities analyst Arthur Stevenson. "It tells us there is nothing fresh out there in fundmentals."
March futures ended $5 a tonne weaker, at $1,362, having ranged from $1,373 to $1,358. May fell $7, to $1,386, while the rest finished $3 to $14 lower.
On the charts, near-term support was seen at $1,358, today's low in the March contract, followed by $1,350. Resistance was pegged at $1,375-$1,378, a gap on the charts.

Fundamentally, General Cocoa said total cumulative Ivory Coast cocoa arrivals through December 7 were "guesstimated" at around 340,000 tonnes compared with an estimated 480,000 tonnes at the same date last year.
The total Ivory Coast main crop is currently estimated at 850,000 to 900,000 tonnes, they said, with reports of scattered rains in the cocoa growing regions expected to benefit the 1997 mid crop.
General Cocoa noted, however, it remains too early for any reliable preliminary estimates.
